applies_why: The judge's stated basis for UNDERDETERMINED is that Matthew 1:20 was answered in two different senses by the two sides, which is the kind of verse-level openness K-S2 addresses.
quote: D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- Challenger answered the conception agency as covenant presence in [DR3] and defender answered the physical source in the womb in [CR2] and [CR3].
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: “A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand”: one reading treats the judge’s use of the two sides’ different senses of Matthew 1:20 to support UNDERDETERMINED as forbidden openness; the other treats it as merely recording party arguments without relying on the verse’s ambiguity.
why: The judge made UNDERDETERMINED rest on two different readings of the single verse Matthew 1:20, but K-S2 says a verse carrying two senses at once is not open and both senses stand.
